title: Systemic Mastocytosis
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE Navigator (NCCN Guidelines Version 3.2026)
provenanceNote: Comprehensive NCCN Guidelines Version 3.2026 clinical navigator for Systemic Mastocytosis (SM). Covers complete clinical algorithm: Diagnostic Workup (bone marrow biopsy with tryptase/CD117/CD25/CD2 IHC, baseline serum tryptase, high-sensitivity KIT D816V mutation allele-specific PCR/ddPCR, myeloid NGS panel for ASXL1, SRSF2, TET2) -> WHO Diagnostic Criteria (Major + 1 minor OR 3 minor) -> B-Findings (burden: BM mast cells >30%, serum tryptase >200 ng/mL, organomegaly without dysfunction) & C-Findings (cytopenias ANC<1k, Hb<10, Plt<100k; hepatomegaly with liver dysfunction/ascites; skeletal osteolyses with fractures; malabsorption) -> Disease Classification: Indolent Systemic Mastocytosis (ISM, 0 C-findings) vs Smoldering SM (SSM, 2+ B-findings, 0 C-findings) -> Advanced Systemic Mastocytosis (AdvSM: Aggressive SM ASM, SM with Associated Hematologic Neoplasm SM-AHN, Mast Cell Leukemia MCL) -> Targeted Therapies: Avapritinib 25 mg daily (rare-mastocytosis-avapritinib Category 1 Preferred for severe/refractory ISM), Avapritinib 200 mg daily (Category 1 Preferred for AdvSM with pre-treatment platelet count >=50k), Midostaurin 100 mg BID with food (rare-mastocytosis-midostaurin Category 1 Preferred for AdvSM with severe thrombocytopenia or avapritinib contraindication), Cladribine, Allogeneic HCT evaluation for fit AdvSM/MCL. References StewardMD Standard Protocols. DRAFT - clinical decision support; physician decides and dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
sourceNote: Structured in accordance with NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology (NCCN Guidelines) for Systemic Mastocytosis Version 3.2026 (July 2026).

a.text: WHO diagnostic criteria for SM: Major criterion (multifocal dense infiltrates of >=15 mast cells in aggregates in bone marrow or extracutaneous tissue) plus >=1 minor criterion, OR >=3 minor criteria. Minor criteria include atypical spindle-shaped mast cells, aberrant CD25/CD2 expression, KIT D816V mutation, and baseline serum tryptase >20 ng/mL (in absence of myeloid neoplasm).

b.text: Avapritinib 25 mg orally once daily is the Category 1 preferred therapy for moderate-to-severe ISM refractory to mediator-directed therapy, based on the PIONEER trial; FDA approved for ISM. Dose engine calculates patient-specific doses; physician decides.

c.text: Avapritinib 200 mg orally once daily is the Category 1 preferred therapy for AdvSM with pre-treatment platelet count >=50 x 10^9/L, based on the EXPLORER and PATHFINDER trials. Obtain baseline head CT/MRI to rule out intracranial hemorrhage risk before starting.

d.text: Midostaurin 100 mg orally twice daily with food is the Category 1 preferred therapy for AdvSM with severe thrombocytopenia (platelets <50 x 10^9/L), intracranial bleeding risk, or avapritinib contraindication.

e.text: Allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) evaluation is recommended for fit patients with AdvSM or mast cell leukemia, particularly refractory disease or rapid progression after KIT inhibitor therapy.

nodes.name: Diagnostic Workup
nodes.title: Systemic Mastocytosis: Diagnostic Workup Checklist
nodes.description: Step 1: Complete diagnostic workup before WHO classification. Secure bone marrow tissue with definitive IHC, run mandatory ultra-sensitive KIT D816V testing, and stage organ burden.
bullets: Complete history (flushing, pruritus, anaphylaxis, syncope, abdominal pain, diarrhea, bone pain) and physical examination (urticaria pigmentosa / maculopapular cutaneous mastocytosis).
Bone marrow aspirate and trephine core biopsy: morphologic examination with Wright-Giemsa and aspirate smears for atypical spindle-shaped mast cells.
Immunohistochemistry panel: tryptase, CD117 (KIT), CD25, CD2, CD30. WHO major criterion: multifocal dense infiltrates of >=15 mast cells in aggregates.
Baseline serum total tryptase (ideally >20 ng/mL minor criterion in absence of myeloid neoplasm; consider hereditary alpha-tryptasemia HaT genotyping if tryptase elevated).

Molecular testing: mandatory ultra-sensitive KIT D816V mutation assay (ASO-qPCR or ddPCR, limit of detection <=0.01% in bone marrow or peripheral blood). Broad myeloid NGS (ASXL1, SRSF2, TET2, RUNX1, CBL, EZH2, NRAS/KRAS) for mutation-enhanced prognostic scoring (MARS / IPSM).
Baseline organ assessment: CBC with differential, CMP (LFTs, albumin, renal), DEXA scan for osteopenia/osteoporosis, abdominal ultrasound or CT for hepatosplenomegaly and lymphadenopathy.

options.label: Diagnostic Workup Reviewed — Proceed to Subtype & Risk Stratification

nodes.name: Disease Classification
nodes.title: Systemic Mastocytosis: Subtype & Risk Stratification
nodes.description: Step 2: Apply WHO diagnostic criteria, then count B-findings (disease burden without dysfunction) and C-findings (organ dysfunction requiring cytoreduction) to classify ISM vs SSM vs AdvSM.
bullets: WHO diagnosis requires Major + >=1 minor criterion OR >=3 minor criteria (major: multifocal dense aggregates of >=15 mast cells; minors: atypical morphology, aberrant CD25/CD2, KIT D816V, tryptase >20 ng/mL).
B-findings (burden, function preserved): bone marrow mast cells >30%, serum tryptase >200 ng/mL, organomegaly (hepato/splenomegaly, lymphadenopathy) without dysfunction.

C-findings (dysfunction, treat): cytopenias (ANC <1k, Hb <10 g/dL, platelets <100k), hepatomegaly with liver dysfunction or ascites, skeletal osteolyses with fractures, malabsorption with weight loss.
Indolent SM (ISM): SM criteria met, 0 C-findings. Smoldering SM (SSM): >=2 B-findings, 0 C-findings. AdvSM: >=1 C-finding present (ASM, SM-AHN, MCL) or >=20% mast cells on bone marrow smear (MCL).
Prognostic layering: mutation-enhanced scores (MARS / IPSM) using ASXL1, SRSF2, TET2 and cytopenias guide intensity of surveillance and transplant referral.

nodes.name: ISM Symptom Burden
nodes.title: ISM: Mediator Symptom Burden
nodes.description: ISM confirmed (no C-findings). Grade mediator-release symptom burden and response to symptom-directed therapy to select continued mediator control versus KIT inhibitor therapy.
bullets: Mild or controlled symptoms: flushing, pruritus, GI cramping, or infrequent anaphylaxis controlled on H1/H2 blockade and trigger avoidance.

Moderate-to-severe symptoms refractory to mediator therapy: recurrent anaphylaxis, syncope, malabsorption, or bone pain persisting despite optimized H1/H2 antihistamines, leukotriene blockade, and cromolyn.
Reconfirm 0 C-findings and review tryptase trend before escalating; ISM with rising burden warrants re-biopsy to exclude progression toward SSM or AdvSM.

nodes.name: ISM Mild Treatment
nodes.title: ISM, Mild Symptoms: Mediator-Directed Therapy
nodes.description: Symptom-directed mediator therapy with anaphylaxis preparedness and bone-health surveillance; no cytoreduction indicated without C-findings.
bullets: H1 antihistamines (e.g. cetirizine or loratadine) plus H2 antihistamines (e.g. famotidine) as the backbone of mediator blockade.
Add leukotriene inhibitor (montelukast) and oral sodium cromolyn for GI symptoms; topical steroids or calcineurin inhibitors for cutaneous lesions.
Epinephrine auto-injector for every patient plus an anaphylaxis action plan; premedication before anesthesia, surgery, and iodinated contrast.
Bone health: calcium/vitamin D, repeat DEXA, and antiresorptive therapy for osteoporosis; avoid NSAID and alcohol triggers where identified.
Surveillance: annual tryptase, CBC, CMP, and symptom review; re-biopsy and re-stage promptly if cytopenias, organomegaly, or tryptase doubling suggest progression.

nodes.name: ISM Refractory Treatment
nodes.title: ISM, Moderate-to-Severe Refractory: Avapritinib 25 mg Daily
nodes.description: KIT inhibitor therapy for ISM with moderate-to-severe symptoms refractory to optimized mediator-directed therapy.
bullets: Avapritinib 25 mg orally once daily, Category 1 Preferred based on the PIONEER trial and FDA approved for ISM; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses and physician decides.
Continue background best supportive mediator therapy during initiation; taper antihistamines only after sustained symptom response.
Monitor platelets, hemoglobin, edema, and cognitive effects; hold and dose-modify per protocol for cytopenias or intracranial symptoms.
Response assessment: validated symptom scores (ISM-SAF), serum tryptase, KIT D816V allele burden, and bone marrow mast cell burden at restaging.
Re-stage for AdvSM (CBC, CMP, imaging, marrow) if cytopenias or organ dysfunction emerge on therapy.

nodes.name: SSM Management
nodes.title: SSM: Monitoring vs Progression
nodes.description: SSM confirmed (>=2 B-findings, 0 C-findings). Distinguish stable high-burden disease on close monitoring from progression toward AdvSM requiring cytoreduction.
bullets: Stable SSM: high mast cell burden (tryptase >200 ng/mL, marrow >30%, organomegaly) but preserved counts, liver function, albumin, and weight.
Progression toward AdvSM: new cytopenia (ANC <1k, Hb <10, platelets <100k), liver dysfunction or ascites, weight loss with malabsorption, or pathologic fracture.
Any suspected C-finding triggers prompt re-biopsy, organ restaging, and AdvSM pathway entry; do not start cytoreduction on B-findings alone.

options.label: Progression: emerging C-finding or rapid burden rise

nodes.name: SSM Monitoring
nodes.title: SSM, Stable: Close Monitoring + Mediator Therapy
nodes.description: Active surveillance of high-burden smoldering disease with mediator control; cytoreduction reserved for documented progression.
bullets: Mediator-targeted therapy as in ISM (H1/H2 antihistamines, leukotriene inhibitor, cromolyn, epinephrine auto-injector) for symptom control.
Surveillance every 3-6 months: CBC with differential, CMP with albumin, serum tryptase, KIT D816V allele burden; annual marrow, DEXA, and abdominal imaging.
Track MARS / IPSM variables (age, counts, ASXL1/SRSF2/TET2 status) at each visit; rising score prompts earlier restaging.
Consider cytoreduction only if a C-finding is documented or burden rises rapidly; stable B-findings alone do not mandate KIT inhibitor therapy.
Counsel on progression symptoms (bleeding, jaundice, ascites, weight loss, fractures) with an explicit return-precautions plan.

nodes.name: SSM Progression Treatment
nodes.title: SSM With Progression: Re-stage as AdvSM, Consider Cytoreduction
nodes.description: Documented or imminent C-finding in SSM: re-stage through the AdvSM pathway and consider cytoreductive therapy.
bullets: Urgent re-staging: repeat marrow with KIT D816V quantification, CBC/CMP, tryptase, and abdominal imaging to confirm the C-finding.
Enter the AdvSM pathway (platelet-stratified KIT inhibitor selection); SSM with a confirmed C-finding is managed as AdvSM.
Bone-directed therapy for new osteolysis or fracture; GI and nutrition support for emerging malabsorption.
Early HCT referral for fit patients whose trajectory suggests aggressive disease, especially with high-risk myeloid co-mutations.
Do not delay AdvSM therapy while awaiting full NGS if a C-finding is clinically evident; send NGS in parallel.

nodes.name: AdvSM Subtype
nodes.title: AdvSM: ASM vs SM-AHN vs MCL
nodes.description: AdvSM confirmed (>=1 C-finding or >=20% mast cells on marrow smear). Subclassify to co-manage the associated neoplasm and set transplant urgency.
bullets: Aggressive SM (ASM): >=1 C-finding (cytopenias, liver dysfunction/ascites, osteolysis with fracture, malabsorption) without associated hematologic neoplasm or leukemic mast cells.

SM with associated hematologic neoplasm (SM-AHN): SM plus a WHO-defined myeloid neoplasm (most often CMML, MDS/MPN, or AML); treat the AHN per its own guideline in parallel with mast cell-directed therapy.
Mast cell leukemia (MCL): >=20% mast cells on bone marrow smear, with or without circulating mast cells (leukemic vs aleukemic); most urgent transplant referral.
All three subtypes proceed to platelet-stratified KIT inhibitor selection; subtype determines co-therapy and HCT timing, not the KIT inhibitor branch.

options.label: Mast cell leukemia (MCL, >=20% mast cells on smear)

nodes.name: AdvSM Platelet Stratification
nodes.title: AdvSM: Platelet & Bleeding-Risk Stratification
nodes.description: Pre-treatment platelet count and intracranial bleeding risk determine avapritinib eligibility versus midostaurin; refractory or rapidly progressive disease routes to salvage and HCT.
bullets: Platelets >=50 x 10^9/L without intracranial bleeding risk: avapritinib-eligible; obtain baseline head CT/MRI first.
Platelets <50 x 10^9/L, intracranial bleeding risk, or avapritinib contraindication: midostaurin pathway with food.
Refractory to KIT inhibitor or rapid progression (worsening C-findings, leukemic expansion): salvage with cladribine and urgent HCT evaluation.

options.label: Platelets <50 x 10^9/L or bleeding risk / avapritinib contraindicated
Refractory / rapid progression on or after KIT inhibitor

nodes.name: AdvSM Avapritinib Treatment
nodes.title: AdvSM, Platelets >=50: Avapritinib 200 mg Daily
nodes.description: First-line KIT D816V inhibitor for AdvSM with adequate platelets and no intracranial bleeding risk.
bullets: Avapritinib 200 mg orally once daily, Category 1 Preferred per EXPLORER and PATHFINDER trials; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses and physician decides.
Mandatory baseline head CT/MRI to rule out intracranial hemorrhage risk; hold for platelet fall below 50 x 10^9/L or any intracranial symptoms.
For SM-AHN, treat the associated hematologic neoplasm per its own guideline in parallel (hypomethylating agent, AML-type, or CMML-directed therapy as indicated).
Response assessment: marrow mast cell burden, serum tryptase, KIT D816V allele burden, C-finding resolution, and spleen/liver volume.
Fit patients, especially MCL: parallel allogeneic HCT referral at initiation; avapritinib response can serve as a bridge to transplant.

nodes.name: AdvSM Midostaurin Treatment
nodes.title: AdvSM, Severe Thrombocytopenia: Midostaurin 100 mg BID
nodes.description: KIT inhibitor therapy for AdvSM with severe thrombocytopenia, bleeding risk, or avapritinib contraindication.
bullets: Midostaurin 100 mg orally twice daily with food, Category 1 Preferred for AdvSM with severe thrombocytopenia or avapritinib contraindication; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses and physician decides.
Antiemetic premedication and GI prophylaxis; monitor QTc, LFTs, cytopenias, and pulmonary symptoms during therapy.
For SM-AHN, treat the associated hematologic neoplasm per its own guideline in parallel with mast cell-directed therapy.

Response assessment: marrow mast cell burden, serum tryptase, KIT D816V allele burden, and C-finding resolution; reassess platelets for potential avapritinib switch if counts recover and bleeding risk resolves.
Fit patients with persistent C-findings: maintain parallel allogeneic HCT referral.

nodes.name: AdvSM Salvage Treatment
nodes.title: AdvSM Refractory / Rapid Progression: Cladribine + HCT Evaluation
nodes.description: Salvage cytoreduction and urgent transplant evaluation for KIT inhibitor-refractory or rapidly progressive AdvSM and MCL.
bullets: Cladribine (2-CdA) cytoreduction for refractory or rapidly progressive disease, with infection prophylaxis and cytopenia support; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses and physician decides.
Urgent allogeneic HCT evaluation for fit patients, especially MCL and SM-AHN with high-risk co-mutations; donor search at salvage decision, not after response.
Re-biopsy with repeat KIT and myeloid NGS to exclude clonal evolution of the AHN component; redirect AHN therapy if the non-mast-cell clone drives progression.
Bridge leukemic MCL with cytoreduction while completing transplant workup; enroll in clinical trial where available.
Best supportive care discussion, including mediator control and bone protection, runs in parallel with salvage planning.
